headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces, but dbt-core can still emit trusted outputs that pathway may consume.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented shared communication channel with pathway, and pathway has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, or filesystem ingestion surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies dbt-core output into pathway prompts, the risk becomes non-none.
IF either agent is connected through a shared filesystem or message queue, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared prompt channel.
Do not pipe dbt-core logs into pathway inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while pathway is local-only with no filesystem read or network egress. The pair does not show a direct leakage path, but if an operator routes warehouse outputs into pathway, sensitive data could be exposed in transformed outputs.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs warehouse rows into files or prompts consumed by pathway, leakage risk increases.
IF pathway is connected to any external sink through an unlisted integration, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid passing warehouse extracts into pathway unless minimized.
Review dbt models for sensitive columns before handoff.
Keep pathway offline from external sinks.
requires-engineering: add column-level redaction before any transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core can call a data warehouse API, but pathway has no write_filesystem, modify_git_state, network_egress, or subprocess capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is not supported.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants pathway write access to the same warehouse or repo, conflict risk becomes non-none.
IF dbt-core is extended with additional write surfaces not listed here, reassess.
mitigations: Keep pathway read-only relative to dbt outputs.
Do not grant shared write access to the same resources.
Document any future shared mutable resource before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs, and pathway may process data pipelines, but pathway has no documented action-taking authority or direct input channel from dbt-core. A cascade is only plausible if an operator feeds dbt outputs into pathway without verification.
conditions: IF dbt-core output is treated as authoritative input by pathway, cascading errors become more likely.
IF pathway is later connected to downstream actuators, reassess upward.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between dbt-core and pathway.
Use schema checks on all transferred outputs.
Keep human review for high-impact transformations.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, while pathway is documented as touching no data classes and has no network egress. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, but any transfer of regulated warehouse data into pathway would need policy review.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and is routed through pathway, compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for any intermediate artifacts.
Avoid sending regulated data through pathway unless approved.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
